scope: Switzerland-wide counts. Job-title search terms are German. No canton or language filter.

data_notes.html: No snapshot for Tuesday 2026-09-29. The collection job could not reach our database and stopped before querying any platform. The platforms only expose live totals, so that week cannot be reconstructed and stays a gap in every series. A Wednesday run (2026-09-30) exists as calibration data and is not part of the series.

Title checks are now per platform. Until now a job title carried one badge, the best score across platforms, and jobscout24.ch had never been sampled. Every platform is now sampled and scored separately. Counts whose title-match share is under 30% on a platform are no longer plotted for that platform; the raw value stays in the tables and downloads, marked as excluded.

Comparable industries reduced from 6 to 5. Agriculture was removed because the jobs.ch category also contains forestry and timber. The interactive charts and the dropdown now use one industry list; before, the bar chart and the other two charts showed different sets.

One method per series. Industry series no longer switch between a platform's own industry filter and values derived from occupation codes. jobscout24.ch industry series therefore start on 2026-09-15, when its native filter was added. Earlier charts showed an occupation-derived value for 2026-09-08 on the same line.

Correction: jobs.ch Energy and Utilities, 2026-09-15. The stored value of 3,843 is withdrawn. The same category read 598 on 2026-09-22 and 539 on 2026-09-30, and the same fault in the platform's category counter was documented for 2026-09-08. The value was never plotted; it is now also removed from the downloads.

Correction: jobscout24.ch Healthcare. The series now uses the platform's own industry filter, like every other jobscout24.ch industry. A plausibility rule had rejected those readings because healthcare is more than 30% of the platform's tagged postings. The rule now compares against the platform's unfiltered total. The published numbers do not change: the occupation-derived reading shown before was identical.

Plausibility checks changed. A reading that moves more than 40% against its recent level is no longer rejected outright. It is held and published only after the next daily reading confirms the new level. Changes of more than 3x need a manual review. Small counts (under 50 postings, or a change of under 30 postings) are exempt, because one employer can move them.
